neighbours.label: the word right after 'worst' or 'worse' (worst of, worst part, worse than): the negative-superlative side of the distinction, where 'best'/'better' stay low
fire: Everyone agreed that the third winter was the worst of the whole decade.
For the players, the worst moment came in the final minute of the match.
Being ignored by your friends is worse than being criticized by them.
The flight was delayed, the hotel was dirty, and worst of all, it rained.
My grandmother says the worst thing about getting old is the loneliness.
The traffic on Friday was even worse than the radio had warned us.
He lost his keys on the worst day possible, right before the interview.
Of all the storms that hit the coast, that one was the worst by far.
quiet: Everyone agreed that the third winter was the mildest of the whole decade.
For the players, the best moment came in the final minute of the match.
Being praised by your friends is nicer than being praised by strangers.
The flight was on time, the hotel was clean, and best of all, it was sunny.
My grandmother says the best thing about getting old is the free time.
The traffic on Friday was much lighter than the radio had warned us.
He found his keys on the best day possible, right before the interview.
Of all the storms that hit the coast, that one was the longest by far.
